newsitem.title: USA: NYC announces $2.7 bln of potential bond sales.
newsitem.headline: NYC announces $2.7 bln of potential bond sales.

text.p: New York City and the city's Water Authority may sell up to $2.7 billion of debt over the next four months, the city's financial adviser said on Wednesday.

Public Resources Advisory Group said New York City expects to sell about $500 million of tax-exempt fixed rate bonds and about $120 million of taxable fixed rate bonds for capital improvements during the week of April 7.
Depending on market conditions, the sale may also include $300 million of tax-exempt fixed rate refunding bonds and $50 million taxable variable rate refunding bonds.
Smith Barney Inc. will be bookrunning senior manager for the fixed-rate tax-exempt bonds, Public Resources said.

The New York City Municipal Water Finance Authority expects to sell about $600 million of tax-exempt fixed-rate bonds for capital improvement purposes during the week of April 28, according to the financial adviser.
J.P. Morgan Securities Inc. is expected to be bookrunning senior manager for that deal.
